cards.text: Friend, meet Zechariah, a prophet. Earlier, God gave him a message for the people: "Return to Me," and "I will return to you" (Zechariah 1:3). Now it's a few months later, in the second year of Darius, king of Persia (Ezra 4:24), and the word of the LORD comes to Zechariah again.

Zechariah looks out into the night and sees a man riding a red horse among the myrtle trees in the hollow, with red, sorrel and white horses behind him. Friend, at night I can't tell my chocolate chips from my raisins, and Zechariah's out here naming horse colors.

cards.question: Zechariah looks out into the night and sees a man on a red horse with more horses behind him. What does he do?

answers.text: He runs to tell the people

cards.text: Zechariah asks, "What are these, my lord?" An angel who is speaking with him replies, "I will show you what they are."

cards.question: Then the man among the myrtle trees explains the horses. The LORD has sent them out, and He sent them to ___ the earth.

cards.text: The riders report back to the angel of the LORD among the myrtle trees: "We have patrolled the earth, and behold, all the earth is at rest and tranquil." Then the angel of the LORD speaks to the LORD of Hosts about Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, and he says the LORD has been angry with them these seventy years.

cards.question: The angel of the LORD has a question for the LORD of Hosts about Jerusalem and the cities of Judah. What does he ask?

answers.text: How long He will withhold mercy from them
When He will send the riders out to them
Why the nations are so angry with them

cards.question: After the angel of the LORD asks how long, the LORD speaks hard and angry words to the angel who is speaking with Zechariah.

cards.text: The angel who is speaking with Zechariah tells him to proclaim a word, and it's straight from the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: The first thing the LORD of Hosts says is about Jerusalem and Zion. How does He say He feels about them?

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts turns to the nations that are at ease.

cards.question: The LORD says He is fiercely angry with the nations that are at ease.
The LORD says, "For I was a little angry…" Then He says what the nations did. What was it?

cards.text: Picture me with a little flour on my apron, and some guy walks by and dumps the WHOLE BAG on my head. The nations piled on like that, and now the LORD says what He's going to do about it.

cards.question: The LORD says He will return to Jerusalem. How will He return?
The LORD says that in Jerusalem, His ___ will be rebuilt.

cards.text: And a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem. I love a measuring line, friend, because I measure dough by eyeballing it, and my cookies come out in three sizes: small, medium and "what HAPPENED here."

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts also says His cities will again stand empty.
The LORD says He will again comfort Zion. What does He say He will do with Jerusalem?

cards.text: Then Zechariah looks up and sees four horns. He asks the angel who is speaking with him, "What are these?"

cards.question: The angel explains the four horns. What did these horns do to Judah, Israel and Jerusalem?

cards.text: Then the LORD shows Zechariah four craftsmen. Four horns that scattered His people, and here comes the WORK CREW.

cards.question: Zechariah asks what the craftsmen are coming to do. They've come to ___ the horns and throw them ___.
The horns had scattered Judah so that no one could raise his head.

cards.text: And these aren't just any horns, friend. They're the horns of the nations that lifted up their horns against the land of Judah to scatter it.
We'll stop here, friend, but Zechariah's night isn't over yet.
